Position Description

The Director of Development Engineering oversees all civil, site, and nuclear engineering activities required to advance Aurora powerhouse sites through development and into construction readiness. Your team produces the technical deliverables — site layouts, basis-of-design packages, geotechnical and environmental assessments, and engineering inputs to permitting — that underpin state/local approvals and NRC licensing (coordinated with Oklo's Environmental & Permitting team), project financing, and construction handoff. Environmental & Permitting and Project Finance are coordinated with Oklo's dedicated teams.
Specific responsibilities may include:

Lead development engineering across all active sites: site layout, civil/grading design, geotechnical investigation, hydrology, and infrastructure planning
Solutions engineering for potential co-located buildings such as advanced manufacturing and data centers
Produce basis-of-design documentation sufficient for project finance due diligence and EPC handoff
Manage third-party engineering consultants and coordinate with Oklo's internal nuclear design team
Provide engineering inputs to NRC licensing and NEPA processes coordinated by Oklo's Environmental & Permitting team
Develop and maintain engineering standards, templates, and quality protocols for the Development organization
Partner with Oklo’s New Product Integration (NPI) team to translate reactor design requirements, siting criteria, and product evolution into site-specific technical constraints and development scope — ensuring early alignment between product design and site realities
Develop and own site constraints packages for each Aurora powerhouse development site, synthesizing geotechnical, hydrological, environmental, grid, and regulatory inputs into a single authoritative technical baseline that governs site selection, design, and permitting decisions
Integrate and quality-control deliverables from civil, geotechnical, environmental, and nuclear engineering consultants — ensuring all third-party work products are consistent, current, and accurately reflected in the site constraints package and project schedule
Own the development engineering schedule and provide cross-functional technical leadership to identify, prioritize, and mitigate technical risks and fatal flaws on project sites — coordinating with Project Development, Transmission & Interconnection, and Oklo’s Environmental & Permitting team to surface issues early and preserve development optionality
Lead structured technical risk reviews at each stage gate, evaluating site constraints packages against go/no-go criteria and escalating unresolved fatal flaw risks to the VP of Development with clear options analysis and recommended disposition
Build and manage a team of engineers across civil/site/electrical and nuclear development disciplines
Provide engineering support for Isotope production facilities, including facility layout, utility infrastructure design, and integration with co-located Aurora powerhouse systems
Lead development engineering for Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses (NLICs), coordinating multi-use site design across power generation, isotope production, and research facility components

Minimum Qualifications:

12+ years in energy, infrastructure, advanced manufacturing or data center project development engineering, with at least 5 years in a leadership role
Strong civil/site engineering background; nuclear project experience highly valued
Experience producing engineering deliverables for project financing and EPC handoff
PE license strongly preferred; experience with DOE or NRC-regulated facilities a significant advantage

Competencies

We are looking for a Director of Development Engineering that is:
Passionate about clean energy 
Passionate about making advanced fission a reality
Willing and able to learn quickly
Eager to work on a dynamic team, receive constructive feedback, and grow with us
Willing to think differently and do things in new ways 
Comfortable in a fast-paced, highly iterative startup environment
Excited to think creatively, critically, and reflectively about the problems they are solving, while not leaning only on what has been done before 
Willing to propose novel and creative solutions to technical problems
An excellent writer who can write in modern active voice, so make your cover letter compelling and write it well!
Able to communicate technical content and results verbally 

Who you are:

A startup person : You aren't driven by titles or hierarchy, and prefer efficiency to excess process. You don't need or expect to have a lot of guidance but you enjoy working in a fast-paced team. If you prefer the culture and feel of a large organization, that is great, but you likely won’t enjoy working with us! There is plenty of important work and plenty of good opportunities with organizations like that.
Motivated : You are self-motivated. You bring an enthusiasm to the team, and imbue a sense of passion that goes beyond clocking in and clocking out. This isn’t about a fake or arbitrary “pieces of flair” mentality or lack of work-life balance! It is about being a part of the vision and feeling a part of reaching team goals.
A team-player : Oklo genuinely is a team. We aren’t about taking credit for ourselves, and we aren’t about pushing blame to others. We do incredible things because we work as a team.
An excellent communicator : We need a person who is not only technically competent but also a clear and upbeat communicator.
Creative : Being creative means that when things fall outside clear scopes or processes or problems arise without clear solutions, you are able to identify it as well as invent ways to solve a problem or fill a need without micromanagement. The successful person in this job will not only be creative, but also enjoy being creative and solving open-ended problems which may change day-by-day.
Detail-oriented : This focus is a big part of excellence, consistency, and quality. Excellent grammar and spelling matter for both good communication as well as the image of the company that we put forward.

Oklo requires remote employees to travel to headquarters (Santa Clara, CA) twice a quarter annually, based on business or team needs, including attendance at team meetings, off-sites, and other company events or gatherings. For the first two weeks of onboarding, employees are required to be in person at headquarters in Santa Clara, CA.

Salary: $225,000-$275,000

Oklo Inc. is developing fast fission power plants to deliver clean, reliable, and affordable energy at scale; establishing a domestic supply chain for critical radioisotopes; and advancing nuclear fuel recycling to convert nuclear waste into clean energy. Oklo was the first to receive a site use permit from the U.S. Department of Energy for a commercial advanced fission plant, was awarded fuel material from Idaho National Laboratory, and submitted the first custom combined license application for an advanced reactor to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Oklo is also developing advanced fuel recycling technologies in collaboration with the U.S. Department of Energy and U.S. National Laboratories.

Pathfinding
: We chart new ground where no path exists by approaching challenges with curiosity, courage, and creativity while navigating ambiguity.

Overview

The earliest years of a child’s life create the foundation for lifelong health, learning, and emotional well-being. At Brookdale Hospital, the HealthySteps Program Director has the opportunity to shape that foundation by leading an innovative, evidence-based program that integrates child development and infant mental health expertise directly into pediatric primary care.

The Program Director provides the strategic, clinical, administrative, and operational leadership necessary to ensure that infants, young children, and their families receive coordinated, family-centered, and developmentally appropriate support in pediatric primary care. The Program Director leads a multidisciplinary team and oversees program quality and fidelity, staff development, grant administration, fiscal performance, clinical operations, data and outcomes reporting, and community partnerships.

HealthySteps, a nationally recognized program of ZERO TO THREE, strengthens the traditional pediatric care model by addressing the developmental, behavioral, social-emotional, and family needs that influence a child’s ability to thrive. HealthySteps at Brookdale Hospital is supported by public and private funding and participates in a multisite, statewide initiative funded by the New York State Office of Mental Health to expand and integrate mental health services within pediatric primary care.

Through collaborative leadership and a commitment to health equity, the Program Director advances Brookdale Hospital’s ability to give children and families—particularly those from historically under-served communities—the strongest possible start in life.

Responsibilities

Leadership and Staff Supervision:

Provide administrative and reflective supervision to a multidisciplinary team of seven (7) staff representing varying disciplines and credential levels, as well as assigned interns and volunteers.
Assign and adjust staff responsibilities to promote operational efficiency, appropriate workload distribution, and maximum delivery of HealthySteps services.
Oversee the HealthySteps’ pediatric residency training program, including curriculum development, delivery, and evaluation.
Establish performance expectations, provide ongoing coaching and feedback, and address performance or conduct concerns in collaboration with Human Resources and departmental leadership.

Monitor expenditures against approved budgets and grant line items.

Recommend budget modifications and reallocations, when necessary, subject to organizational and funder approval.
Ensure responsible stewardship of public and private program funds.

Program Oversight

Provide strategic and operational leadership for the implementation, maintenance, and continued development of the HealthySteps program.

Establish, monitor, and evaluate program goals, workflows, performance measures, service-delivery standards, and patient outcomes.

Ensure the timely and accurate submission of departmental, organizational, regulatory, and funder reports.
Ensure program operations comply with applicable federal and state regulations, grant requirements, organizational policies, professional standards, and patient privacy requirements.
Identify opportunities for performance improvement and lead corrective action and quality-improvement initiatives when appropriate.
Collaborate with pediatric providers and other members of the interdisciplinary care team to support coordinated, family-centered, and developmentally appropriate care.

ArtWorks for Milwaukee is a nonprofit organization that empowers Milwaukee-area youth through paid internships in the arts, creative workforce development, and meaningful partnerships with artists, businesses, and community organizations. By connecting young people with professional opportunities to develop artistic and career-ready skills, ArtWorks helps prepare the next generation of creative leaders while strengthening Milwaukee's arts and cultural community.

The Executive Director serves as the chief executive officer of ArtWorks and reports directly to the Board of Directors. Working in close partnership with the Board, the Executive Director provides strategic, financial, and operational leadership while serving as the organization's primary ambassador to donors, partners, and the broader community.

This is an opportunity for a collaborative, entrepreneurial leader who enjoys building relationships, strengthening organizations, and creating sustainable impact. The Executive Director will guide the organization's strategic direction while leading fundraising efforts, cultivating partnerships, strengthening organizational systems, and supporting a small, committed staff team.

ArtWorks is intentionally investing in administrative and financial support so the Executive Director can focus on organizational leadership, fundraising, community engagement, and long-term organizational sustainability.

Foster a collaborative, inclusive, and mission-driven organizational culture.
Represent ArtWorks as the organization's primary spokesperson and community ambassador.
Identify opportunities for organizational growth, innovation, and strategic partnerships.

Cultivate, solicit, and steward individual donors.

Support a collaborative organizational culture that prioritizes communication, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Ability to think strategically while also executing day-to-day organizational priorities.
Experience working collaboratively with a Board of Directors or other governing body.
Commitment to equity, youth development, and the transformative power of the arts.

Preferred

Experience supervising and coaching staff.

Experience with CRM systems, donor management platforms, or organizational technology.

Organization Overview:
Phi Kappa Tau Fraternity
Phi Kappa Tau is entering an exciting period of growth and opportunity, as it builds on a 120-year tradition of championing brotherhood, learning, ethical leadership, and exemplary character. The fraternity serves 4,300 undergraduate members at approximately 80 chapters, and has about 100,000 alumni members. While the Phi Kappa Tau fraternity experience begins on campus, it lasts a lifetime: throughout their lives, members form meaningful friendships, find opportunities to lead and serve, and build powerful personal and professional networks.

Phi Kappa Tau Fraternity (the Fraternity) is a 501(c)(7) nonprofit headquartered in Oxford, Ohio with a national staff of approximately 15 professionals and an elected Board, known as the National Council. It supports campus chapters and members with leadership development, educational programming, recruitment, chapter operations, national events, and alumni programs. The Fraternity is funded from undergraduate member fees, event registration fees, and an educational grant from the Phi Kappa Tau Foundation (the Foundation). The Foundation is an affiliated 501(c)(3) tax-exempt nonprofit organization with its own Board of Trustees and professional staff. The Fraternity collaborates with the Foundation on communications, events, alumni programming, and other areas where the two organizations have shared interests.
In its next phase of growth, the Fraternity’s strategic plan, Building the Phi Kappa Tau Experience , centers on strengthening existing chapters, expanding to new campuses, deepening undergraduate and alumni engagement, broadening leadership and learning opportunities, and creating greater value for members throughout their lives.

This is a once-in-a-generation opportunity to help shape the Phi Kappa Tau member experience at a time when meaningful personal connection and ethical leadership are more valuable than ever before. The next CEO will bring Phi Kappa Tau’s recognized leadership education to a new generation of students while strengthening the bonds of brotherhood among all members.

Position Summary:
Chief Executive Officer

Phi Kappa Tau seeks an energetic, growth-minded Chief Executive Officer to champion its mission, support its members, and lead the organization into its next era of impact. Reporting to the National Council, the CEO will lead the execution of the organization’s strategic plan and serve as a highly relational leader who is equally comfortable working both in and on the organization. They will build credibility across a diverse community, from undergraduate members and young staff to alumni volunteers and university administrators.

Internally, the CEO will lead a national staff and oversee a complex organization with an annual budget of approximately $3 million. This leader will bring financial discipline and operational rigor, with particular attention to budgeting, forecasting, accounts receivable, and financial reporting. They will provide the mentorship, coaching, structure, and accountability needed to help both early career and experienced staff members grow and perform at a high level.
Externally, the CEO will focus on growth and engagement across the Fraternity. They will help existing chapters grow and thrive while executing our strategy to expand to new campuses. As a strong trust-builder and communicator, they will strengthen relationships with university administrators, engage Phi Kappa Tau’s alumni, expand its volunteer network, and create more opportunities for lifelong connection to the Fraternity.

The ideal candidate will bring an appreciation for fraternity and lifelong brotherhood and exposure to collegiate fraternal organizations – whether through membership, professional leadership, volunteer service, or board involvement. Experience within business, membership organizations, or nonprofits is likewise valued. This is an opportunity to pair seasoned leadership with fresh thinking to shape the future of Phi Kappa Tau for generations to come.

Key responsibilities

Strategic Leadership, Governance & Growth

Partner with the National Council on strategy, policy, and governance, providing timely reporting on organizational performance, finances, strategic plan progress, and emerging risks.
Lead implementation of Phi Kappa Tau’s strategic plan, establishing measurable goals and translating priorities into clear organizational and staff work plans.
Develop and execute strategies to grow undergraduate membership, strengthen retention, and expand Phi Kappa Tau to new campuses.
Identify, execute, and evaluate new programs and approaches that advance strategic priorities, using data to understand results and scale what works.

Organizational, Financial & People Leadership

Lead the Fraternity’s approximately 15-person staff, including org chart design, hiring, performance management, compensation, professional development, and mentorship of both early-career and experienced professionals.
Provide overall financial stewardship, including annual budgeting, cash flow management, fee-setting for programs and membership, collections, balance sheet management, and ongoing financial performance monitoring.
Strengthen organizational systems and processes, using data and emerging technology (including AI) to improve efficiency, reporting, decision-making, and the member experience.
Oversee proactive risk prevention, disciplinary issues, legal matters, and crisis response, stepping in directly to support chapters and volunteers when significant issues arise.

Chapters, Members & Volunteers

Ensure chapters receive responsive, high-quality support and resources that help them recruit and retain members, develop leaders, and operate effectively.
Build and sustain Phi Kappa Tau’s volunteer network by recruiting and engaging volunteers, matching individuals with meaningful opportunities, and supporting volunteer boards and committees.
Oversee national events and educational programming, including National Convention and leadership and learning programs.
Improve the member experience by modernizing existing programs, services, communications, and digital resources, and finding innovative new ways to create value for undergraduate and alumni members.

External Relations, Communications & Partnerships

Serve as a visible public face and ambassador for Phi Kappa Tau at chapter, alumni, national, and interfraternal events and within the broader fraternity and sorority community.
Strengthen relationships with host colleges and universities, including direct engagement with administrators when chapters need support or challenges arise.
Partner with the Foundation Executive Director on joint initiatives and collaborative planning.
Lead consistent, transparent, multi-channel communication with undergraduate members, alumni, volunteers, parents, university partners, and other stakeholders.

Leadership & Competency Expectations

Dynamic Communicator & Trusted Bridge-Builder

An engaging leader who can connect authentically across the Phi Kappa Tau community. They will adapt their style to different audiences, listen with empathy, and skillfully navigate difficult conversations, whether navigating sensitive issues, supporting a chapter leader through a challenge, or advocating for the fraternity’s interests. A compelling storyteller and ambassador, they can also command a room, inspire new members, and represent Phi Kappa Tau with confidence before a range of audiences.

Coach, Mentor & Team Builder

Leads with a coaching mindset, creating an environment where a small, relatively young staff can learn, take ownership, and pursue ambitious goals. This leader will recognize that some team members are early in their careers and will provide the mentorship, feedback, professional development, and clear expectations the staff needs to succeed. They will build accountability while fostering a culture of trust, collaboration, and shared purpose.

Innovative & Growth-Minded Leader

Brings fresh thinking to how Phi Kappa Tau grows and creates meaningful value for its members. This leader will challenge longstanding approaches and critically evaluate processes, resources, and programs with an eye toward what today’s students and alumni need. They will strengthen existing chapters, expand to new campuses, and explore ways to diversify revenue sources.

Decisive, Adaptable & Collaborative Leader

Comfortable leading within a complex environment where decision-making involves varied stakeholders: student members, alumni, elected leadership, volunteers, and university administrators. This leader will listen to different perspectives and build buy-in while also knowing when it is time to make a decision and move forward. They are comfortable recognizing gaps in expertise and leveraging volunteers and outside experts. They will be responsive and consistent in their follow-through, working effectively with the National Council and volunteer leaders while navigating change and competing priorities.

Location, Compensation and Benefits

Phi Kappa Tau’s headquarters is located in Oxford, Ohio, and the organization welcomes candidates based in or around the Greater Cincinnati area. There is a strong preference for a CEO who can maintain a regular and visible presence in the Executive Offices, working alongside the staff and providing in-person mentorship, particularly to early-career team members. The role includes regular travel of approximately 10 - 25% to engage with chapters, members, alumni, volunteers, university partners, and attend national events, as well as occasional evening and weekend commitments.
Salary is commensurate with experience and qualifications. Phi Kappa Tau offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental and vision coverage, paid time off, employer-paid life and disability insurance, and a 401(k) plan with an employer match.

Organization Overview:

For more than 50 years, AgeGuide Northeastern Illinois has worked to ensure that people can age with confidence, purpose, connection, opportunity and choice. AgeGuide brings together public resources, community partners, and a powerful regional network to strengthen the systems and services that support older adults, veterans, and their caregivers across a region with a growing aging population. Its work includes advocacy, community needs assessments, program development, grant administration, service coordination, and the advancement of policies that support people in aging well and remaining engaged in their communities.

With approximately $30 million in annual resources, AgeGuide operates largely as a pass-through funder and steward of public resources rather than a direct-service organization. Primarily funded through the federal Older Americans Act and the Illinois Department on Aging, AgeGuide directs more than $26 million annually to 35+ community-based partners providing nutrition, transportation, caregiver support, legal assistance, health promotion classes, benefits counseling, social connection, and other essential services. AgeGuide also directly provides a Veteran Directed Care program through a partnership with several Veterans Affairs Medical centers, helping veterans receive the support they need to remain in their homes and communities.

Position Summary:

AgeGuide Northeastern Illinois is seeking a Chief Executive Officer to lead the organization into its next chapter. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the CEO will lead a staff of approximately 35, including five direct reports, and provide strategic, operational, and external leadership. The CEO will also maintain strong working relationships with the Illinois Department on Aging and the Illinois Association of Area Agencies on Aging, ensuring alignment with state guidelines and navigating the legislative and political environment affecting aging services. The next CEO will inherit an organization with a strong track record of impact, experienced leadership, deep community relationships, and a respected network of funded partners, with an opportunity to build on that momentum as the aging-services landscape continues to evolve.

The CEO will listen first and lead with curiosity, taking time to understand AgeGuide’s staff, Board members, programs, and funded partners while valuing the institutional knowledge and relationships that have contributed to its success. Working closely with the Board, Advisory Council, leadership team, staff, and partners, the CEO will translate AgeGuide’s Strategic Plan and Area Plan into clear priorities and measurable results. The CEO will value and advance diversity across the Board and staff, ensuring that a broad range of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives informs the organization’s leadership and decision-making.
They will provide engaged, hands-on executive oversight across programs, finance, human resources, technology, compliance, internal controls, and risk, while empowering an experienced leadership team.

As AgeGuide’s chief ambassador and advocate, the CEO will strengthen the organization’s role as a regional planner, funder, convener, quality-assurance partner, and advocate, while expanding its visibility and influence across the region and beyond. They will cultivate relationships with elected officials, government agencies, healthcare organizations, community leaders, funded providers, and peer aging organizations. With much of AgeGuide’s funding rooted in federal and state programs, the CEO will champion public policy and continued investment in aging services, while identifying opportunities to diversify revenue through innovation, strategic partnerships, and expanded fee-for-service programs.
For a seasoned leader passionate about improving the experience of aging, this is an opportunity to build on AgeGuide’s strong foundation and shape an ambitious next chapter for the organization and the communities it serves.

Key responsibilities

Strategic Leadership & Execution:
Translate AgeGuide’s Strategic Plan and Area Plan into clear priorities, measurable goals, and action, while positioning the organization to respond to emerging needs and opportunities.
Organizational & Operational Leadership:
Provide executive oversight across programs, finance, human resources, technology, compliance, and risk, ensuring strong systems, accountability, and organizational performance.
Government Relations & Advocacy:
Cultivate strong relationships with elected officials and government agencies and advocate at the local, state, and federal levels for policies and resources that advance the needs of older adults and caregivers.
Funded Partner Network & Service Quality:
Strengthen AgeGuide’s network of funded partners through trusted relationships, ongoing engagement, and effective contract and performance oversight; work alongside providers to address challenges and ensure high-quality, person-centered services.
Public Funding & Compliance:
Ensure federal and state resources are administered in accordance with the Older Americans Act, Illinois requirements, grant conditions, and applicable reporting standards; maintain executive accountability for compliance monitoring, audit readiness and response, and corrective action plans.
Aging Policy & Regulatory Leadership:
Provide leadership in interpreting and implementing federal and state statutes, regulations, and aging-related programs; lead high-stakes regulatory interpretation and negotiation with the Illinois Department on Aging.
External Partnerships & Visibility:
Elevate AgeGuide’s visibility and influence by building strategic relationships across healthcare, government, nonprofit, philanthropic, and community sectors and identifying opportunities for collaboration and innovation.
Financial Stewardship
: Ensure responsible stewardship of AgeGuide’s public and private resources through strong internal controls, sound financial management, audit readiness, and effective risk management.
Healthcare Contracting & Revenue Diversification:
Lead AgeGuide’s healthcare contracting and business development strategy to diversify revenue through partnerships with the VA, CMS, Managed Care Organizations (MCOs), and other public and private entities. Bring expertise in healthcare financing, government contracting, value-based partnerships, and market development to drive sustainable growth and expand AgeGuide’s impact.
Board & Advisory Council Partnership
: Maintain transparent, collaborative relationships with the Board of Directors and Advisory Council, providing timely strategic information, supporting effective governance, recruitment, and engagement.
People, Culture & Organizational Capacity
: Lead and develop a strong senior leadership team, foster an inclusive and age-friendly workplace, strengthen staff development and succession planning, and ensure the organization has the structure and talent to deliver on its priorities.
Data, Technology & Innovation
: Strengthen the use of data, technology, and emerging tools to inform resource allocation, evaluate outcomes, improve organizational effectiveness, and identify new approaches to serving a rapidly changing aging population.
Aging-Sector Leadership
: Maintain an active leadership presence within the Illinois Association of Area Agencies on Aging (I4A) and other state and national aging networks, sharing best practices, strengthening cross-agency collaboration, and bringing emerging ideas and successful models to AgeGuide.
Organizational Resilience
: Lead the organization through funding delays, regulatory changes, provider instability, political shifts, and other disruptions, while maintaining continuity of critical programs and services.

Leadership & Competency Expectations

Visionary Strategist & Pragmatic Operator

A forward-looking leader who can see the broader forces shaping aging services while maintaining a disciplined focus on execution. They will translate AgeGuide’s mission and strategic priorities into clear plans, measurable results, and sustainable programs. Comfortable navigating complex funding, regulatory, and service-delivery systems, they will balance innovation with sound judgment, financial stewardship, and operational accountability.

Dynamic Communicator & Trusted Bridge-Builder

An engaging and credible leader who can connect authentically with older adults, caregivers, staff, Board members, funded partners, policymakers, and community leaders. They will listen with empathy, communicate complex issues clearly, and navigate difficult conversations with candor and respect. A compelling storyteller and ambassador, they will elevate AgeGuide’s visibility, strengthen its influence, and build partnerships across diverse communities and sectors.

Compassionate, Inclusive & Courageous Leader

A mission-driven leader who brings integrity, emotional intelligence, humility, and resolve to their work. They will value the knowledge and experience of staff and partners, foster an inclusive and accountable culture, and create the conditions for people to succeed. Resilient and adaptable, they will make thoughtful but timely decisions, address difficult issues directly, and keep the needs of older adults and caregivers at the center of the organization’s work.

Location, Compensation and Benefits

This is a hybrid role based in AgeGuide’s Lombard office.

The anticipated salary range for this full-time, salaried position is $130,000 to $160,000,
commensurate with experience and qualifications. AgeGuide offers generous paid time off and holidays, as well as a comprehensive health and retirement benefits package.

omputational E

lence), an industrial partnerships program within the National Center for Computational Sciences (NCCS). This position can be on-site, remote, or hybrid. NCCS provides state-of-the-art computational and data science infrastructure coupled with dedicated technical and scientific professionals tackling large-scale S&T challenges across a broad range of scientific domains for accelerating scientific discovery and engineering advances. NCCS hosts the Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility, one of DOE’s National User Facilities which operates Frontier, the nation’s first exascale supercomputer.

Purpose

The Program Director of ACCEL will collaborate across other sections in the division and directorate to strategically advance the ACCEL industry partnership program so that it continues to be recognized as the premier industrial partnerships program for leadership computing within the DOE. Consistent with ORNL’s culture, historical leadership, and continued vision to be the world’s premier R&D institution for computational science, the Program Director will foster relationships with ambitious industry partners so that they can collaborate with ORNL’s flagship computational ecosystem.

The candidate must be able to interact comfortably with both corporate and laboratory researchers, laboratory management, and industry C-suite executives who often are the decision makers that permit their research teams to use national laboratory computing systems to solve competitively important corporate science and engineering problems. ACCEL’s Program Director also serves as an ambassador for the lab and the leadership computing facility to industry and may be the first person to ever inform a company that they may qualify for access to OLCF resources.

Major Duties/Responsibilities:

Grow the industrial partnerships program by identifying and cultivating new industrial users for the OLCF resources.
Understand the different allocation programs to apply for time on the OLCF systems and their requirements and be able to discuss these clearly with potential new industrial users so they can determine if they might qualify to receive an allocation.
Understand the legal agreements required to use the OLCF resources and be able to explain these generally in advance to potential new users. (Note that if an award is made, OLCF has an experienced on-boarding team that will lead a new user through each step.)

Nurture current OLCF industrial users to ensure they continue to bring their large-scale computational problems to OLCF.
As relationships with industry users grow, identify potential areas for scientific collaboration between industry and the researchers within OLCF and the broader computing directorate, and bring relevant parties together to explore and decide on specific collaborative projects.

Understand the OLCF science impact business model and be able to explain it to potential users so they understand the context and rationale for the different allocation programs and legal agreements.
Be prepared to work with OLCF leadership to develop new programs and opportunities to expand industrial usage as laboratory and DOE needs and requirements change.
Organize visits to OLCF/CCSD for company researchers/executives to meet with lab researchers/executives to better familiarize the company with OLCF/CCSD and the lab and identify new areas to work together.
Work with OLCF communications team to develop stories for the OLCF and DOE websites about industrial accomplishments using OLCF resources.
Provide management support to the Division Director for an industry and federal agency computing roundtable that reports to him and his counterpart at the Argonne Leadership Computing Facility.

BS degree with minimum 10 years relevant experiences.
Experience in partnership development and relationship management in/across the public and/or private sectors.
Commitment to advancing scientific missions and national competitiveness.

Preferred Qualifications:

Basic understanding of the DOE national laboratory system and preferably its variety of user facilities, including its high-performance computing user facilities.
Working knowledge of why and how companies across a spectrum of industries use high performance computing.
Comfortable operating in a matrixed environment.
Excellent organizational and interpersonal skills.
Enthusiastic first-approach skills.
While you don’t need to be a computer or computational scientist, you must be comfortable acting as a bridge between potential and current industrial users of OLCF leadership computing resources and the diverse experts within OLCF that can speak with users specifically about their science/engineering challenges.

Security, Credentialing, and Eligibility Requirements: For employment at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL), a Real ID compliant form of identification will be required. Additionally, ORNL is subject to Department of Energy (DOE) access restrictions. All employees must also be able to obtain and maintain a federal Personal Identity Verification (PIV) card as mandated by Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12) and Department of Energy (DOE) Order 473.1A, which requires a favorable post-employment background investigation.

To obtain this credential, new employees must successfully complete and pass a Federal Tier 1 background check investigation. This investigation includes a declaration of illegal drug activities, including use, supply, possession, or manufacture within the last year. This includes marijuana and cannabis derivatives, which are still considered illegal under federal law, regardless of state laws.

The SPLC is seeking a Deputy Director, Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning who is passionate about social justice!

The Deputy Director, MEAL manages MEAL support throughout the program/project life cycle with a particular focus on program design, monitoring and strengthening SPLC's community accountability efforts.

Who You Are

Strategic, analytical, and systems-oriented
— Connects MEAL practices to organizational strategy and impact, using data and evidence to inform decision-making and strengthen effectiveness.

Equity- and community-centered
— Centers community voice, lived experience, and accountability while recognizing how power and systemic inequities shape evaluation, learning, and outcomes.

Collaborative and influential leader
— Builds trust across teams, communicates effectively with diverse stakeholders, and influences organizational decision-making without relying solely on positional authority.

Curious, rigorous, and courageous
— Asks difficult questions, challenges assumptions, surfaces uncomfortable findings, and approaches complex issues with intellectual rigor and sound judgment.

Learning and improvement-oriented
— Builds a culture of reflection, experimentation, shared learning, and continuous improvement while helping teams translate insights into meaningful action.

Adaptable, results-oriented capacity builder
— Navigates ambiguity and the evolving nature of social justice work while strengthening staff and organizational capacity to use data, evidence, and learning to achieve meaningful, equitable, and sustainable impact.

What You'll Do

Lead
the development and implementation of a MEAL strategy and approach that is responsive to social justice work and values and builds an organization that regularly uses data for learning, improvement and measuring impact.

Provide
guidance and review for MEAL products to ensure technical soundness as well as clarity and accessibility for non-MEAL audiences.

Manage
MEAL team collaboration with other departments to design MEAL frameworks and capture data that informs decision-making and measures the impact of work.

Manage
collaboration across different departments to support the implementation of community-based accountability practices and tools and to implement in the organization's programs, projects, initiatives, and activities.

Conduct
in-person and remote training on MEAL related topics, and travels as needed.

Facilitate
project brainstorming, design, strategy and planning sessions, and provides technical assistance on MEAL throughout all stages of the project life cycle to programs and teams across the organization.

Support
evaluations and research around the impact of SPLC's work.

Manage
a team of MEAL staff members by hiring, training, mentoring, coaching, assigning duties, setting and monitoring performance and development goals, and conducting performance reviews.

Perform
other duties as required or assigned which are reasonably within the scope of the duties in this job classification.

Minimum Qualifications

We are committed to equitable hiring practices, therefore you must meet the minimum qualifications to be considered for the role.

Minimum seven (7) years of monitoring, evaluation, accountability & learning experience;
At least five (5) years of directly managing staff; and
Minimum of bachelor's degree in political science, sociology, measurement & evaluation, social work, education, public policy or related fields.

Compensation & Benefits

At Johnson & Johnson, we believe health is everything. Our strength in healthcare innovation empowers us to build a world where complex diseases are prevented, treated, and cured, where treatments are smarter and less invasive, and solutions are personal. Through our expertise in Innovative Medicine and MedTech, we are uniquely positioned to innovate across the full spectrum of healthcare solutions today to deliver the breakthroughs of tomorrow, and profoundly impact health for humanity. Learn more at jnj.com.

As guided by Our Credo, Johnson & Johnson is responsible to our employees who work with us throughout the world. We provide an inclusive work environment where each person is considered as an individual. At Johnson & Johnson, we respect the diversity and dignity of our employees and recognize their merit.

Job Function

Job Sub Function

Job Category

All Job Posting Locations:

Spring House, Pennsylvania, United States of America

Job Description

About Innovative Medicine

Our expertise in Innovative Medicine is informed and inspired by patients, whose insights fuel our science-based advancements. Visionaries like you work on teams that save lives by developing the medicines of tomorrow.

Join us in developing treatments, finding cures, and pioneering the path from lab to life while championing patients every step of the way.

Learn more at https://www.jnj.com/innovative-medicine

About Oncology

Our expertise in Innovative Medicine is informed and inspired by patients, whose insights fuel our science-based advancements. Visionaries like you work on teams that save lives by developing the medicines of tomorrow.

Our Oncology team is focused on the elimination of cancer by discovering new pathways and modalities to finding treatments and cures. We lead where medicine is going and need innovators with an unwavering commitment to results.

Join us in developing treatments, finding cures, and pioneering the path from lab to life while championing patients every step of the way.

Learn more at https://www.jnj.com/innovative-medicine

We are searching for the best talent for an Executive Director, Discovery Oncology position. You will be responsible for leading and guiding the Oncology discovery research in selected cancer indications. The Executive Director, Discovery Oncology defines and executes on the strategy for Oncology Discovery. This individual will develop a portfolio of therapeutics addressing core pathways in Oncology from project concept through to entrance into clinical trials.

You Will Also Be Responsible For

Leads a global group of approximately 20-40 people (including regular FTEs, temporary contractors and postdoctoral fellows), guiding their science with an emphasis on scientific quality and rigor.
In partnership with Oncology leadership, including TA head, clinical, strategic and functional leaders, defines the scientific strategy for the TA and develops a portfolio of assets for solid cancer indications.
As a Disease Area Stronghold discovery leader executes on the strategy for the end-to-end Oncology portfolio.
Creates an environment that values innovation, leadership, scientific excellence, urgency, and personal accountability.
Manages resource allocations across programs, included shared resources across labs.
Proactively influences across functional areas and external partners to align project activities with strategic goals.
Establishes internal and external collaborations to facilitate execution of Discovery strategy.
Partners with external collaborators and innovation centers to evaluate and discover new approaches, technologies, and targets in support of the Oncology portfolio.
Partners with business development to evaluate external assets and bring new molecules into the pipeline.
Runs collaborations with both academic and industry partners.
Provides management oversight including personal talent development, training, coaching and guidance to discovery scientists.
Ensures compliance with all J&J training, while ensuring safe laboratory working practices for self and reports.
Ensures consistent experiments/data generation for target validation and progression through discovery stages.

You Will Be Responsible For The Following Leadership Priorities

Oversee and influence the initiation and the progression of multiple small and large molecules as well as cell therapy discovery research programs that result in the identification of Clinical Candidates.
Set and execute the scientific strategy for solid tumor indication(s).
Act as an ambassador for the respective Discovery Portfolio with frequent interactions with senior internal and external stakeholders.
Demonstrate excellent managerial skills to enable his/her global team to deliver on their objectives and to develop their careers.
Provide input on hiring, promotions, resources and budget allocations within the department.
Direct the proper use and implementation for new technology to establish long-term research plans.
Identify novel scenarios and nascent scientific/technical opportunities in a specific scientific area.
Communicate overall strategy of the projects to others including senior leadership.
Build collaborative relationships with and influence key stakeholders; internally and externally.
Create a high-performance work environment that values innovation, leadership, scientific excellence, urgency, and personal accountability.
Attract and cultivate talent.

Qualifications / Requirements

PhD with deep content knowledge in Oncology.
15+ years of demonstrated leadership and drug discovery experience in the area of Oncology, preferably in solid malignancies.
Experience:
Solid background in drug discovery across modalities (small, large molecules, cell therapy), including immune therapies.
Background in cellular, molecular and/or immune tumor biology with a good understanding of the therapeutic landscape in Oncology.
Strong record of leading programs to the identification of Clinical Candidates.
Strong track record of publications in the field.
Broad scope of impact beyond individual projects, eg leading research platforms, target classes, etc.
Strong external network and recognized as an expert in the field by peers.
Demonstrated competence for team leadership and/or people skills to manage a team with members in different continents.
Leading or being part of a significant organization change.
Heavy influencing across organization boundaries and without direct authority.
Enterprise thinking.
Detail-oriented as well as being able to see the big picture.
Excellent oral and written communication skills; able to effectively present scientific data and concepts to international standards.
Shaping and articulating a vision that inspires, engages, and brings others along a change journey.
Ability to attract and develop talent.

At ACT, Your Work Makes a Difference

Education has power – a power that changes lives forever. It creates opportunities that lift up individuals, their families, and sparks societal change that echoes through generations to come. From our grassroots we have fought the good fight for equity in education, and we remain devoted to helping anyone who struggles to access that power. This is what matters to us and we must do better -- we’ve never been more sure of our purpose.

ACT team members are part of an organization dedicated to a mission that has never been more important: Helping people achieve education and workplace success. Advancing that mission within our organization, by helping our team members achieve education and workplace success of their own, is core to our values. ACT values a diverse workplace and is committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable environment in which every team member has an opportunity to grow.

We want our team members to have the well-being and confidence they need to do their best work, in an environment where both they and ACT thrive. To support this, our total rewards include company paid life insurance, medical, dental, vision, flexible health and dependent spending accounts, 401(k) retirement savings with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and so much more. You can find a comprehensive list of our benefits here.

We are seeking a Program Director of Major Accounts and District Partnerships
to help us fulfill that mission.

ACT's largest and most complex district partnerships require a different kind of leader. The Program Director of Major Accounts and District Partnerships
owns a focused portfolio of the nation's largest school districts with responsibility for new business capture, growth within existing relationships, and driving measurable impact at scale. This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who knows these districts, has credibility at the leadership table, and can navigate the full complexity of large-district procurement and decision-making.

The finalist will be hired at the salary and level commensurate with their qualifications. For this position, we anticipate offering an annual salary in the range of $115,000 to $125,000.
ACT manages salaries within the range based on relevant factors including, skills, experience, and internal equity. This position is incentive eligible.

Location:
This is a remote position, based in the United States.
Visa:
Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for visa sponsorship.

What You Will Be Working On

A named account list of approximately 50 of the nation's largest school districts
A plan that identifies, qualifies, and pursues high-value opportunities across assigned accounts, including new solution adoption, expanded utilization, and contract growth with measurable outcomes
Direct engagement with district senior leadership — Superintendents, Associate Superintendents, and Cabinet-level decision makers, and boards of education — to align ACT solutions with district priorities and initiatives
Develop and execute comprehensive, multi-year account plans for each assigned district, working with account and program management teams for account support
Lead ACT's response to large district RFPs — driving solutioning, costing, and requirements development
Navigate complex procurement processes involving multiple stakeholders, funding sources, and budget cycles
Advise districts on post-adoption data utilization and best practices to drive measurable outcomes
Inform internal product, pricing, and delivery decisions based on the unique needs and scale of major districts
Collaborate with state partnership and field sales teams to align on strategy, share intelligence, and coordinate on shared accounts
Represent ACT at national and regional events, building and maintaining a strong presence among large-district leadership networks

This could be the job for you if you have (minimum requirements):

At least 7 years of significant experience selling to or working within large K-12 school districts
Have an established network of senior district leaders, you either have these districts as current or former clients or you’ve held a senior role inside one; ability to influence and engage individuals at the district senior leadership and decision-making level from day one
Deep knowledge of district priorities, budget cycles, funding mechanisms, and procurement processes
Proven track record closing complex, multi-year deals in competitive environments
Command of the K-12 assessment landscape — policy, competitive dynamics, and how districts evaluate and adopt assessment solutions
Elite negotiation, consultative selling, and executive presentation skills
Ability to gather and use competitive intelligence to create strategies that advance and/or protect ACT’s interests
Ability to work effectively and build relationships with individuals within the organization
Strong communication skills including ability to communicate effectively across all levels in the organization
Strong analytical abilities and the ability to determine logical solutions to complicated problems
Ability to set goals and priorities and manage to completion
Access to a central hub airport and ability to travel at least 25% of time
Bachelor’s degree in Education, Business or a related area of study; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

It’s a Plus If You Have

Direct experience with college and career readiness programs, assessments, or related solutions
Familiarity with state-level education policy and how it shapes district decision-making
Experience coordinating across internal teams (product, operations, finance) to structure large, customized deals

About ACT

When ACT was founded in 1959, it disrupted the assessment industry with a new approach to helping students better understand their readiness so they could take steps to improve it. By leveraging our expertise and authority in assessment and research, we will again disrupt the industry—helping more people learn, better measure their progress, and improve their navigation through life’s transitions.

More than ever before, ACT is fulfilling its mission of helping people achieve education and workplace success. We’re doing it by pushing the boundaries of learning innovation through the work of our people, who we call team members because we’re all in this together.

We know transformation does not come without challenge. That’s why ACT invests in a variety of experiences for team members to strengthen their connections, explore ideas, learn from customers, and celebrate success.

Learn more about working at ACT at act.org!
